# computesphere_environment_variables (Resource)

Manages an environment's shared variables, one resource per environment: the plain variables every deployment in the environment inherits (a deployment's own value for a key wins). This resource owns the whole set: a variable set elsewhere and not listed here is removed. Changing a variable restarts the deployments that inherit it; a service whose deploy policy is `approval` gets the change with its next deploy unless a project admin makes it. Keep credentials out of plain variables.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Shared variables every deployment in the environment inherits. A
# deployment's own value for a key wins. This resource owns the whole set.
resource "computesphere_environment_variables" "example" {
  environment_id = "e1f2a3b4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab"

  variables = {
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
    REGION    = "us-east-1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment the variables belong to. Changing it removes the variables from the old environment and sets them on the new one.
- `variables` (Map of String) Variable name to value. An empty map removes every shared variable of the environment.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The environment id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by environment id.
terraform import computesphere_environment_variables.example e1f2a3b4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
```
